newsitem.title: GERMANY: German companies shifting R&D abroad - DIW.
newsitem.headline: German companies shifting R&D abroad - DIW.

text.p: German companies are shifting more of their research and development efforts abroad, primarily to the U.S., the DIW economic research institute said on Wednesday.
In many cases, the expansion is made by buying research labs in other countries. German firms spent 8.8 billion marks on research abroad in 1995.
"German companies have been boosting their foreign presence, but overseas direct investment in relation to foreign trade is still low compared to the U.S., Britain and France," DIW said in a report.
Chemicals firms are particularly active within the trend, accounting for 4.5 billion marks of the outlays, it said.
"A further increase ... can be expected," it said.
Siemens, Bayer, BASF and Hoechst top the list.
The U.S. attracted 2.45 billion marks of the total in 1994.

Foreign research investment in Germany, by contrast, has been steady for years, totaling eight billion marks and employing 32,000 persons in 1995. U.S. car and machinery makers are among the big foreign investors in German research.
